title: Learning to Route and Schedule LLMs from User Retrials via Contextual Queueing Bandits
summary: Formulates joint LLM routing and request scheduling as a contextual queueing bandit in which an unsatisfied user retrying a query serves as implicit negative feedback, avoiding explicit ratings. A Thompson-sampling algorithm with decaying forced exploration achieves sublinear routing regret while keeping queues stable, and is evaluated on offline routing datasets and real WildChat conversation logs.
key_idea: Treat user retrials as free implicit feedback to learn query-to-LLM routing online under queueing dynamics.
relevance_rationale: Online routing learned from implicit production-style feedback (retrials); directly fills the implicit-feedback gap for routers.
found_via: query: abs:"bandit" AND abs:"LLM" AND abs:"routing"

title: UniScale: Adaptive Unified Inference Scaling via Online Joint Optimization of Model Routing and Test-Time Scaling
summary: Unifies model routing and test-time-scaling choices into a single action space and learns the joint policy online as a contextual bandit with LinUCB plus explicit cost modeling. Reports better quality-cost trade-offs than routing-only or TTS-only baselines in dynamic inference settings.
key_idea: Learn routing and test-time compute jointly online with a LinUCB contextual bandit.
relevance_rationale: Online bandit over combined model-choice and compute-budget actions; transferable to agent step configuration.

title: GreenServ: Energy-Efficient Context-Aware Dynamic Routing for Multi-Model LLM Inference
cost_reduction_reported: Compared with random routing, 22% higher accuracy with 31% lower cumulative energy across five tasks and 16 open LLMs; 71.7% average accuracy on RouterBench
summary: Routes each query among 16 open LLMs with a contextual multi-armed bandit that uses lightweight query features and learns online from partial feedback on accuracy and energy. It needs no offline calibration and new models can be added without retraining.
key_idea: Contextual bandit routing that optimizes accuracy against energy and onboards new models online.
relevance_rationale: Online partial-feedback routing with cold-start for new models; code released.
found_via: query: abs:"bandit" AND abs:"LLM" AND abs:"routing"

title: Policy Regret for Embedding Model Routing: Contextual Bandits with Low-Rank Experts
summary: Formalizes routing queries across multiple embedding models as an adversarial contextual linear bandit with low-rank experts and shows that standard regret notions are misspecified or intractable for this setting. Proposes a log-quadratic policy class and a policy-gradient algorithm with policy-regret guarantees under bandit feedback.
key_idea: Policy-regret theory for online model routing under bandit feedback with low-rank expert structure.
relevance_rationale: Theory for online routing under partial feedback; embedding-model setting rather than generative LLMs.

title: CUPID in the Model Zoo: Online Matchmaking for Selecting Your Dream LLM
summary: Treats choosing an LLM for a user as interactive active learning: a dueling-bandit algorithm shows pairs of model responses, collects the user's preference, and updates a belief over latent preferences. A belief-aware UCB rule trades off exploration against user-specified cost and time budgets, validated with simulations and human studies.
key_idea: Dueling-bandit matchmaking that learns which LLM a user prefers from pairwise feedback under a budget.
relevance_rationale: Arena-style pairwise feedback used online for model selection; per-user rather than per-query.

title: Online Conformal Abstention for Factuality Control Under Adversarial Bandit Feedback
summary: Proposes ExAUL, an online conformal abstention method that controls false discovery rate when the deployed system only receives partial (thumbs-style) feedback on answered queries, possibly from a non-stationary or adversarial stream. A conversion lemma turns bandit regret into an FDR bound, and a feedback-unlocking trick extracts extra signal from the abstention structure.
key_idea: Online risk-controlled answer/abstain gating learned from partial user feedback with FDR guarantees.
relevance_rationale: Fills the online conformal / risk-controlled deferral gap; the abstain decision maps directly onto an escalate decision.
found_via: query: abs:"thumbs" AND abs:feedback AND abs:LLM

title: Online Learning-to-Defer with Varying Experts
summary: Introduces an online multiclass learning-to-defer algorithm for streaming data where the pool of experts changes and feedback is observed only for the chosen action. Gives regret bounds for true deferral loss that scale with the number of models and experts.
key_idea: Learning-to-defer under bandit feedback with a time-varying expert pool.
relevance_rationale: Online deferral with changing experts and partial feedback is the theoretical core of online cascades with model churn.
found_via: query: learning to defer online bandit feedback

title: Cost-Ordered Feasibility for Multi-Armed Bandits with Cost Subsidy
summary: Studies multi-armed bandits with cost subsidy, where the goal is to minimize cost while keeping reward within a tolerance of the unknown best arm. Derives instance-dependent lower bounds and the Cost-Ordered Feasibility algorithm, which pools samples across arms to test whether a cheap arm is good enough.
key_idea: Bandit algorithm for picking the cheapest arm that is near-best in quality.
relevance_rationale: Exactly the objective of cheap-model-first online routing; generic bandit theory.

title: Cache me if you Can: an Online Cost-aware Teacher-Student framework to Reduce the Calls to Large Language Models
venue_or_source: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
cost_reduction_reported: Reports significant operating-expense savings with only slightly lower performance on intent recognition and sentiment analysis (GPT-3.5/GPT-4 teachers)
summary: Proposes an online teacher-student framework in which a cheap local model is trained on LLM responses as they arrive and gradually answers more queries itself, calling the LLM only when needed. Gives a method to tune the call criteria and measure the cost-performance trade-off on business classification tasks.
key_idea: Distill an LLM into a cheap student online from live calls and route to the student when it is confident.
relevance_rationale: Online learning from live traffic to cut LLM calls; directly applicable to repetitive enterprise subtasks.

title: Adapter-Augmented Bandits for Online Multi-Constrained Multi-Modal Inference Scheduling
cost_reduction_reported: Up to 14.18% higher reward than state-of-the-art baselines across budget regimes on a composite multimodal benchmark
summary: Schedules multimodal LLM requests across heterogeneous backends whose costs vary over time, using an adapter-based reward predictor, a primal-dual constraint handler for multiple long-horizon budgets, and a two-phase explore-exploit scheduler. Provides regret bounds under multi-dimensional knapsack constraints.
key_idea: Online constrained bandit routing across backends with time-varying costs and multiple budgets.
relevance_rationale: Online budget-paced routing with non-stationary costs.

title: Latency-Quality Routing for Functionally Equivalent Tools in LLM Agents
cost_reduction_reported: +2.18 pp F1 over SW-UCB on web-search load benchmark; up to +18 pp accuracy over SW-UCB on StrategyQA high-heterogeneity setting
summary: Addresses agents that can call the same tool type through several equivalent providers differing in latency, reliability and quality. A contextual-bandit router ranks providers by expected answer quality per service cycle, combining capacity-aware scores with query-specific quality estimates and LLM-judge feedback without gold labels.
key_idea: Online contextual bandit for tool/provider choice inside agents using judge feedback and latency-as-capacity.
relevance_rationale: Step-level online routing inside agents under runtime load, learning without ground truth.

title: You Cannot Pick a Provider From the Price List: Market-Aware Routing for Open-Weight LLM Inference
cost_reduction_reported: Certification moved live traffic from a premium anchor provider to a substantially cheaper certified endpoint (matched quality)
summary: Measures live inference endpoints across providers serving the same open-weight models over several waves and finds that quality, latency and availability vary widely and are not predicted by price, and that the map drifts over time. Proposes FACET, an online provider router that certifies per-provider, per-task feasibility and fails safe to an anchor provider.
key_idea: Same-model provider routing with online feasibility certification under drifting provider quality.
relevance_rationale: Real endpoint measurements show drift; online safe routing design is directly usable in gateways.

title: When Is the Same Model Not the Same Service? A Measurement Study of Hosted Open-Weight LLM APIs
cost_reduction_reported: In two counterfactuals, routing lowers Qwen3-32B cost by 37.8% and raises DeepSeek-V3.2 throughput ~90% relative to direct official access
summary: A measurement study of hosted open-weight LLM APIs using sampled request logs, provider metadata and continuous latency measurements from a routing platform in Q4 2025. Shows that the same model behaves as different, time-varying services across providers and that routing over provider-model-task-time tuples can lower cost.
key_idea: Hosted models are time-varying services; routing must track provider-level drift.
relevance_rationale: Production-log evidence on non-stationarity of the action set a router chooses from.

title: (Why) Is My Prompt Getting Worse? Rethinking Regression Testing for Evolving LLM APIs
venue_or_source: 2024 IEEE/ACM 3rd International Conference on AI Engineering – Software Engineering for AI (CAIN)
summary: Case study showing that silent updates and deprecations of LLM APIs cause regressions in downstream prompts (toxicity detection). Argues that regression testing for LLM APIs needs new approaches because of fuzzy correctness, prompt brittleness and non-determinism.
key_idea: LLM API updates silently regress downstream behavior, requiring dedicated regression testing.
relevance_rationale: Model-swap drift is a core risk for any learned router or config; motivates continuous re-evaluation.

title: How is ChatGPT's behavior changing over time?
venue_or_source: Special Issue 5: Grappling With the Generative AI Revolution
summary: Compares March and June 2023 versions of GPT-3.5 and GPT-4 on several tasks and finds large behavior changes, such as GPT-4 prime identification falling from 84% to 51% accuracy. Highlights the need for continuous monitoring of LLM services.
key_idea: The same API model can change substantially over months.
relevance_rationale: Canonical evidence for non-stationarity in the arms a router selects among.

title: Privacy-Preserving Data Drift Detection and Recovery for Large-Scale LLM Applications via Proxy Representations
summary: Presents ProxyDrift, which measures drift between production traffic and offline evaluation sets using non-PII proxy descriptors produced by LLM classification of interactions, and refreshes evaluation sets with synthetic queries generated to match. Deployed for an application serving hundreds of millions of users, it also links proxy distributions to user satisfaction.
key_idea: Privacy-preserving drift monitoring and eval-set refresh from proxy representations of production traffic.
relevance_rationale: Production-scale method to keep offline evaluation (and thus router training data) aligned with live traffic.

title: Reinforcement Learning from User Feedback
cost_reduction_reported: 28% increase in Love Reactions in live A/B tests
summary: Trains a reward model P[Love] to predict whether a response will receive a lightweight positive user reaction in production and uses it alongside helpfulness and safety objectives in policy optimization. Shows P[Love] predicts future user behavior offline and raises positive feedback in live A/B tests, while noting reward-hacking risks.
key_idea: Reward model trained on sparse binary production user reactions, validated by live A/B tests.
relevance_rationale: Production evidence that implicit user signals can be modeled offline and validated with A/B tests; same machinery could score routes.

title: DRIFT: Learning from Abundant User Dissatisfaction in Real-World Preference Learning
summary: Observes that deployments produce abundant implicit dissatisfaction signals (users refining or correcting) but few explicit positives, and proposes DRIFT, which anchors preference training on dissatisfaction examples and samples positives from the evolving policy. Reports up to +7.61% WildBench task score and +12.29% AlpacaEval2 win rate at 14B over base models.
key_idea: Learn from plentiful dissatisfaction signals in real logs instead of scarce positive labels.
relevance_rationale: Shows how regenerations and corrections in production logs become a usable learning signal.

title: Leveraging Implicit Feedback from Deployment Data in Dialogue
summary: Uses publicly released BlenderBot deployment conversations to learn from implicit signals such as the length, sentiment and reactions of the following user turn. Human evaluation shows improvements, but some proxies such as conversation length push the model toward controversial outputs.
key_idea: Next-user-turn signals from deployment logs act as implicit quality labels, with proxy-hacking risks.
relevance_rationale: Early production-data study of implicit feedback proxies and their failure modes.

title: CausalRM: Causal-Theoretic Reward Modeling for RLHF from Observational User Feedbacks
summary: Defines observational reward modeling from user feedback such as clicks, copies and upvotes and identifies two problems: label noise and self-selection of which responses receive feedback. CausalRM adds a noise-aware surrogate loss and propensity-style reweighting to learn unbiased reward models.
key_idea: Debias reward models trained on observational user feedback with causal corrections.
relevance_rationale: Selection-bias correction is needed to train routing quality predictors from production thumbs data.

title: ImplicitRM: Unbiased Reward Modeling from Implicit Preference Data for LLM alignment
summary: Learns reward models from implicit feedback that has no definite negatives and whose propensity to be observed varies by response. Stratifies samples into latent groups and derives an unbiased learning objective.
key_idea: Unbiased reward learning from positive-only, propensity-biased implicit feedback.
relevance_rationale: Same issue arises when using production signals to train routers.

title: Correcting Selection Bias in Sparse User Feedback for Large Language Model Quality Estimation: A Multi-Agent Hierarchical Bayesian Approach
summary: Shows that averaging thumbs feedback in production can misestimate system quality by 40-50 points because feedback arrives mainly from the tails. Proposes a hierarchical Bayesian, topic-stratified correction that estimates per-topic selection and quality, plus drift signals, and evaluates it under simulated biases on UltraFeedback.
key_idea: Correct thumbs-feedback selection bias with topic-stratified hierarchical Bayes before using it as a quality metric.
relevance_rationale: Practical guide to making sparse thumbs data usable for monitoring or route evaluation.

title: Deployment-Centered Evaluation: Predicting Query-Level Rejection Risk in a Clinical LLM System
signals_used: deployment context (department, provider type, model used)
summary: Trains a pre-response classifier, inside an EHR-embedded clinical LLM system, that predicts before generation whether the user will reject the response, using query content and deployment context. A prospective 4.5-month evaluation gives AUROC 0.719, and the authors estimate value for guardrail triggering and abstention.
key_idea: Pre-generation predictor of user rejection trained on sparse real deployment feedback.
relevance_rationale: Real production quality predictor that runs before generation; the same design can drive routing or escalation.

title: RouteJudge: An Open Platform for Reproducible and Preference-Aware LLM Routing
summary: An online platform where several routing strategies each pick a model for the same query, and anonymous pairwise user preferences between the resulting responses are attributed back to the routers. Logs query, decisions, responses, preferences, cost and latency, and ships ORBIT, a toolbox for implementing and submitting routers.
key_idea: Arena-style live preference evaluation at the router level rather than the model level.
relevance_rationale: Closest thing to an A/B/interleaving harness for routers; logs are reusable for off-policy learning.

title: Hybrid Preferences: Learning to Route Instances for Human vs. AI Feedback
cost_reduction_reported: Hybrid human/LM mixture yields better reward-model performance than either source alone while reducing human annotation
summary: Routes each preference instance to human or LM annotation by training a performance-prediction model that estimates downstream reward-model quality for a given mix. Releases MultiPref (10K instances with both label types) and shows generalization to three other datasets.
key_idea: Predict where human labels add value and route only those instances to humans.
relevance_rationale: Performance-prediction-driven routing of costly feedback; relevant to budgeting labels for router training.

title: Reward Model Routing in Alignment
summary: Selects one reward model per query from a pool during RLHF, combining an offline multi-task router trained on preference data with an online Bayesian Thompson-sampling selector that addresses cold start and exploration.
key_idea: Offline-warm-started, online Thompson-sampling routing among reward models.
relevance_rationale: Offline-to-online router template; applied to reward models rather than generators.

summary: Defines deployment-time learning, in which agents improve from experience without changing weights, and implements it as CASCADE, an evolving episodic case memory whose reuse is framed as a contextual bandit with no-regret guarantees.

summary: Learns online which query-rewrite strategy to apply per query, using a contextual bandit over semantic features and a calibrated reward, to reduce hallucination in closed-source models. Finds no single rewrite policy is best and some static ones are worse than none.

summary: Optimizes the prompts of a fixed multi-agent workflow under a tight evaluation budget by treating the problem as a bandit with UCB exploration, a graph neural network to capture coupling induced by topology, and coordinate ascent to make the search linear rather than exponential.

title: BOAD: Discovering Hierarchical Software Engineering Agents via Bandit Optimization
summary: Discovers a hierarchical SWE agent by treating candidate sub-agents as bandit arms whose reward is their helpfulness when collaborating, allowing efficient exploration under limited evaluation budgets. The discovered 36B system ranked second on SWE-bench Live at evaluation time.
key_idea: Multi-armed bandit search over sub-agent designs for hierarchical agents.
relevance_rationale: Bandit-driven agent configuration search with credit to sub-agents.

title: Compositional Online Learning for Semantic Data Processing Systems
cost_reduction_reported: Learning components compose to an 11.4x upper bound on per-row LLM cost reduction for a representative conjunction-filter workload, reduced to a realistic ~8x after self-selection, sample-budget shrinkage and selectivity drift
summary: Argues that LLM calls in semantic data processing are slow enough to hide online learner updates inside each round-trip, and builds compositional online learning: memoization, an online filter-ordering learner and an online per-batch cascade-routing learner. A production case study in Snowflake Cortex AISQL decomposes per-row LLM cost by component.
key_idea: Compose online learners (caching, ordering, cascade routing) at the LLM call boundary in production.
relevance_rationale: Production online cascade learning with explicit cost decomposition, including drift effects.

title: Learning to Assign Prediction Tasks to Agents with Capacity Constraints
summary: Studies sequential learning of which agent (human or AI model) should handle each prediction task when each agent can take only a fraction of tasks. Gives a theoretical characterization and explore-exploit policy-learning algorithms that beat non-contextual baselines on tabular, image and text tasks.
key_idea: Contextual explore-exploit assignment of tasks to capacity-limited agents.
relevance_rationale: Capacity-constrained online routing, as with rate-limited frontier models.

title: From Myopic Selection to Long-Horizon Awareness: Sequential LLM Routing for Multi-Turn Dialogue
summary: Moves LLM routing from single-turn to multi-turn dialogue by running MCTS over dialogue branches induced by different model choices, then training a lightweight routing policy on the high-return trajectories. The policy routes per turn without online search and improves task success and the cost trade-off over single LLMs and routers.
key_idea: Learn a per-turn sequential routing policy from search-generated trajectories with delayed rewards.
relevance_rationale: Sequential, delayed-reward routing is the multi-turn analogue of step-level agent routing.

title: OLIVIA: Online Learning via Inference-time Action Adaptation for Decision Making in LLM ReAct Agents
summary: Adds an explicit decision layer to ReAct agents, modeling final action selection as a contextual linear bandit over candidate actions with frozen hidden states as context. It updates online from action-level feedback during deployment and outperforms static ReAct and prompt-based adaptation on four benchmarks.
key_idea: Online bandit layer over agent action selection learned during deployment.
relevance_rationale: Deployment-time online learning at the step level, not cost-targeted.

title: Causal Methods for LLM Development and Evaluation

summary: Position and tutorial paper (KDD 2026) arguing that many LLM development questions, including whether to route a prompt to a larger or smaller model under cost limits, are causal. It reviews how confounded logs, biased judges and non-stationary deployment call for causal inference and off-policy methods.
key_idea: Routing and evaluation from logs should be treated as causal inference.

title: Autoregressive Diffusion World Models for Off-Policy Evaluation of LLM Agents
summary: Estimates the value of a new LLM agent policy in multi-turn environments using only pre-collected trajectories, by learning a latent diffusion world model whose per-step denoising is guided by the evaluated agent. Alternating agent and world-model steps avoids the compounding errors of autoregressive world models.
key_idea: Off-policy evaluation of LLM agents with an agent-guided diffusion world model.
relevance_rationale: Direct OPE for agent policies from logs, the core method needed to vet agent configuration changes offline.

title: Optimal Sequential Annotations for Off-Policy Evaluation
summary: Shows how to spend a limited budget for expert reward annotation in sequential OPE when cheap LLM-judge labels are biased, using doubly robust OPE with missing rewards and variance-optimal annotation probabilities. Motivated by casenotes from a homelessness services nonprofit.
key_idea: Variance-optimal choice of which logged steps to label expertly for doubly robust OPE.
relevance_rationale: Label-budget allocation for evaluating logged policies when rewards come from judges.

title: When is Off-Policy Evaluation (Reward Modeling) Useful in Contextual Bandits? A Data-Centric Perspective
summary: Proposes DataCOPE, a data-centric framework that forecasts how accurate off-policy evaluation will be on a given logged dataset, identifies subgroups where OPE is unreliable, and compares data-collection strategies.
key_idea: Assess whether a logged dataset can support OPE for a target policy before trusting it.
relevance_rationale: Diagnoses when router or config logs are adequate for OPE.

summary: Studies fine-tuning LLMs on historical observational outcomes such as conversion rates instead of A/B test data, showing that naive training learns spurious correlations. Proposes DeconfoundLM to remove known confounders from the reward signal, evaluated on real datasets.
key_idea: Observational outcome logs need deconfounding before use as LLM training signal.

title: Which LLM for Which Work? Budgeted Model Allocation under Uncertain Evaluation
cost_reduction_reported: On paid software tasks, better information about model quality yields more savings than further optimization of the assignment
summary: Frames a company assigning LLMs to recurring workloads under a fixed budget as a knapsack whose quality table is uncertain because models are rarely compared on the same work and scores are proxies. key_idea: Certify a budgeted model-to-workload assignment under uncertain, proxy-based evaluation and spend evaluation where it changes the decision.

title: V_0: A Generalist Value Model for Any Policy at State Zero

summary: Trains a generalist value model that predicts the expected success of any model on an unseen prompt by conditioning on a history of that model's instruction-performance pairs instead of fitting parameters. Used to allocate GRPO rollout budgets and, at deployment, as a router.
key_idea: Predict per-prompt success of any model from its performance profile and route by it.
relevance_rationale: Performance prediction that adapts to new models without retraining; used as a router.

title: Evaluating Confidence-Gated Retrieval with Matched Trajectory Replay
summary: Proposes matched trajectory replay, a protocol that fixes candidate answer states, evidence, budgets and action costs so different confidence-to-action policies can be compared on the same agent trajectories. key_idea: Compare agent gating policies by replaying matched trajectories with fixed costs.
relevance_rationale: Replay-based evaluation method for agent decision policies.

title: When Agents Disagree With Themselves: Behavioral Consistency as an Uncertainty Signal for LLM Agents
summary: Shows that the number of distinct action sequences an agent produces across repeated runs is a black-box uncertainty signal: consistent tasks reach 82-87% accuracy versus 41-65% for inconsistent ones. Selective answering when three runs agree gives 87-88% accuracy at 54-62% coverage.
key_idea: Run-to-run behavioral consistency as an agent success predictor.
relevance_rationale: Cheap success signal usable for agent-level deferral.

title: Calibration Is Not Control: Why LLM-Agent Oversight Needs Intervention
summary: Argues that agent oversight should target the expected gain from intervening rather than failure probability, since prefixes with equal risk may differ in recoverability. Introduces prefix branching to measure intervention advantage and shows the mismatch with risk prediction.
key_idea: Estimate intervention advantage, not failure risk, to decide when to intervene in agents.
relevance_rationale: Relevant to deciding when to escalate an agent step to a stronger model.

title: What Does a Routing Oracle Measure Under Stochastic Decoding? Coupling, Scorer Choice, and Single-Commit Ceilings
summary: Shows that the hindsight oracle used in routing benchmarks is not the same decision class as a router that commits to one model before seeing outputs under stochastic decoding. Distinguishes single-commit ceilings from union probabilities and audits frozen correctness tensors from 11 models.
key_idea: Routing oracles under stochastic decoding overstate the achievable gain of single-commit routers.
relevance_rationale: Clarifies what can be identified when learning or evaluating routers from logged outcomes.

title: Resample or Reroute? Recoverable Stopping Debt Without Identified Action Selection
cost_reduction_reported: In a 152-query MBPP+ study, fixed escalation to Qwen2.5-14B exceeds leave-one-out 7B resampling by +2.882 pp after 7B rejection
summary: Treats choosing between resampling and rerouting after a weak verifier as an identification problem because correctness is hidden, and orders three gates (recoverable stopping debt, action support, held-out selector value) that must pass before claiming a learned selector helps.
key_idea: Gated identification test before claiming a resample-vs-reroute selector adds value.
relevance_rationale: Rigorous treatment of counterfactual claims in escalation decisions.

title: BARouter: A Budget-adaptive Online Large Language Model Router Framework
summary: An online router for LLM serving that adjusts its policy per query from estimated quality, query cost and live budget consumption, so it adapts to different initial budgets and shifting query distributions without manual tuning. Proves sublinear regret and reports outperforming baselines across budget levels.
key_idea: Budget-adaptive online routing with regret guarantees under shifting query distributions.

title: Transcending Cost-Quality Tradeoff in Agent Serving via Session-Awareness
cost_reduction_reported: Comparable response quality to GPT-4o at 16.5% of the cost; 1.8x quality improvement relative to the tradeoff curve
summary: AgServe is an agent-serving system with a session-aware server that improves KV-cache reuse, a client that cascades models within a session from real-time quality assessment, and a dynamic GPU scheduler. Agents can pick and upgrade models during a session, reaching GPT-4o-level quality at a fraction of the cost on real testbeds.
key_idea: Session-aware per-round model cascading plus KV-cache management for agent serving.
relevance_rationale: Per-round model selection inside agent sessions with large reported savings; systems-level evidence.
